business_descriptor: {business}, a free informational and referral service that helps people understand whether their health insurance covers addiction and mental-health treatment and connects them with treatment options — not a treatment provider or insurance company itself
local_angle: in-network treatment availability in the local city and state, typical wait times and options nearby, and how state insurance-parity rules shape the addiction-treatment benefits a given carrier must provide
tone: compassionate, hopeful, and stigma-free; clear and practical about how to use insurance benefits to get help; empowering rather than fear-based, clinical, or salesy; written for someone who may be scared or in crisis
guardrails: {business} is a free informational and referral service — never present it as a treatment provider, clinic, doctor, or insurance company. Do not give medical advice, diagnose, or make clinical claims about addiction or treatment outcomes. Do not guarantee insurance coverage, plan approval, specific benefit amounts, deductibles, or out-of-pocket costs — coverage depends on the individual plan, so always direct the reader to verify their own benefits. Carriers (Aetna, Cigna, etc.) are named only to match what people search; never claim affiliation, endorsement, partnership, or in-network status with any carrier, and note that all carrier names and logos are trademarks of their respective owners. Do not promise sobriety, recovery, or success rates. Do not state specific prices as fact. Never provide legal or insurance-broker advice. Use non-stigmatizing, person-first language. Include a crisis-safety note where appropriate (e.g. call or text 988, or 911 for emergencies). Where the site connects callers with advertising partners, be transparent about that.
